question.text: When SIAB considers an allegation of professional misconduct against an SIA who has a prior warning / censure on record for a similar default, the repeat element typically:

answer.text: Results in automatic debarment without hearing - hearing is waived for repeat offenders.
Triggers a compulsory three-year debarment irrespective of severity.
Is ignored - each proceeding starts de novo with no reference to past record.
Is treated as an aggravating factor in determining sanction, moving the proceeding toward suspension / cancellation rather than warning / censure.

explanation.text: The Logic: In disciplinary jurisprudence, a prior record of similar misconduct is treated as an aggravating factor when determining sanction. The decision-maker typically moves from the lower end of the sanction menu (warning, censure) toward the higher end (suspension, cancellation) when repeat conduct is established. Hearing is not waived — the principles of natural justice continue to apply at every stage. The Trap: Option A (automatic debarment without hearing), Option C (ignoring past record entirely), and Option B (a compulsory fixed-period debarment regardless of severity) each over- or under-shoot the calibrated, case-by-case approach used in disciplinary practice. Note: The specific repeat-misconduct aggravation, warning/censure-to-suspension/cancellation escalation, and fixed/automatic debarment rules are not described in the cited Social Impact Assessors Certification Examination Workbook (January 2026) pages 113-114, 141, 5, 213 or 220. The workbook only states that disciplinary cases/sanctions carry negative weight in SRO empanelment and outlines general SEBI penalty/adjudication powers. The framing above reflects general regulatory and disciplinary-law practice.
